correctness.rationale: For all integers h,m>=2, let d=(h−1)m, s=2R−d, a_i=s−2r_i, and x=r_i−r_j. The signed opposite-color half-peak utility after a red i/blue j cross-part swap yields |a_j−2|<|a_i| and |a_i+2|<|a_j| with a_j=a_i+2x. Their squared strict inequalities force x>=2 and −x−1<a_i<1−x; since a_i is integral, a_i=−x and hence s=r_i+r_j; conversely these values satisfy both strict inequalities. Within-part exchange changes neither part count nor neighborhoods; same-color exchange cannot strictly benefit both. The potential sum r_i² falls by 2(x−1)>=2, proving finite improvement and floor(hm²/2) step bound. For h=3, E_ij is r_i+r_j+2r_k=2m and |r_i−r_j|>=2; Vandermonde gives |E_ij|=A_m−B_m, two-event intersections J_m, and triple intersection is empty, proving N_m=2^(3m)−3(A_m−B_m−J_m). U~Bin(2m,1/2) and V~Bin(m,1/2) independent give mean 2m, variance 3m/2 and lattice span 1; local CLT P(U+2V=2m)=1/sqrt(3πm)+O(m^-1). All diagonal and double-event exclusions have probability O(m^-1), implying P(not equilibrium)=sqrt(3/(πm))+O(m^-1). Independent canonical-profile direct-neighborhood experiments verified (h,m)=(3,2),(3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(4,2),(5,2); separate count values N_m=52,458,3196,28568. The finite tests corroborate rather than prove universal parameters.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural if-and-only-if classification of bilateral improvements on a natural, dense complete multipartite family, plus an exact labeled three-part equilibrium enumeration with quantified inverse-sqrt instability frequency. The contrast between enormous absolute numbers of unstable configurations and their vanishing random-color proportion is a meaningful mathematical feature beyond a generic FIP or tiny numerical check. Equal-part and symmetry assumptions are motivated by game payoffs and network communities, not arbitrary slices. Further questions about fixed-composition or heterogeneous parts remain open; no paper-sized downstream theorem is required.
